title: Do you know what's actually on air? End-to-end testing for Liquidsoap radio pipelines
abstract: In radio and streaming systems, control-plane truth and audio-plane truth are not the same thing. A webhook can fire, metadata can update, and downstream systems can believe the live source is active while the listener briefly hears the wrong source or a transition glitch. This talk presents a practical end-to-end testing method for Liquidsoap-based radio pipelines that verifies what actually went on air. The approach is to connect to the stream like a listener, record the real Icecast output, decode it, and analyze the recording afterwards. By assigning distinct sine-wave frequencies to controlled test inputs, ffmpeg bandpass filters and silence detection can prove which source was audible in which time window. I will cover the failure mode that triggered this work, why event-level assertions were insufficient, how the spectral fingerprinting approach works, and the unexpected harmonic distortion problem caused by the processing chain itself. The result is a practical workflow for testing source transitions, live handoffs, dropouts, and dead air from the listener’s point of view.
